subject: Mathematics: Analysis & Approaches

stem: A drink has temperature T(t)=18+2.4t-0.12t^2 degrees C, 0<=t<=20.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Find T(0) and T(15).

parts.label: b
parts.html: Find when T first reaches 26 degrees C.

parts.label: c
parts.html: State the interval when T>26.

questions.title: Quadratic temperature model
solution: T(0)=18 and T(15)=27. Solving 18+2.4t-0.12t^2=26 gives t=4.23 or 15.8. It first reaches 26 at 4.23 min, and T>26 for 4.23<t<15.8.

stem:
The table gives cumulative frequencies for 52 student heights.
(a) Estimate the median by linear interpolation. [2]
(b) Convert to class frequencies. [2]
(c) Estimate the mean using class midpoints. [3]
questions.title: Cumulative frequency and grouped mean
solution: The median is the 26th value. Between 165 and 170 cm, CF rises from 20 to 36, so median=165+(6/16)(5)=166.875 cm. Frequencies are 2,6,12,16,12,4. The midpoint total is 8660, hence mean=8660/52=166.5 cm.

stem: A differentiable function has f'(x)=x^2-2x-3. Find the interval on which f is decreasing. [4]
questions.title: Intervals of decrease
solution: f'=(x-3)(x+1). This upward-opening quadratic is negative between its roots, so f decreases for -1<x<3.

stem: A Ferris wheel has radius 18 m, centre 21 m above ground and period 6 min. A rider begins at the lowest point.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Find a cosine model h(t)=a-b cos(ct), using radians.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Express it as a sine model using the smallest positive phase shift.

questions.title: Sinusoidal modelling
solution: The midline is 21, amplitude 18 and angular speed 2pi/6=pi/3. Thus h=21-18cos(pi t/3). Since cos u=sin(u+pi/2), h=21-18sin((pi/3)(t+3/2)); the smallest positive shift is 3/2 min.

stem: Let g(x)=x^3-4x+1. Its stationary points are A (maximum) and B (minimum), and the chord AB passes through (0,1).

parts.label: a
parts.html: Find A and B.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Find the exact area between the chord and curve from x=0 to B.

questions.title: Stationary points and area
solution:
g'=3x^2-4, so x=+/-2/sqrt(3). A=(-2/sqrt(3),1+16/(3sqrt(3))) and B=(2/sqrt(3),1-16/(3sqrt(3))). The chord has equation y=1-8x/3. On 0<=x<=2/sqrt(3), chord-curve=4x/3-x^3. The area is
[2x^2/3-x^4/4]_0^(2/sqrt3)=4/9.

stem: Adult heights X are normal with mean mu and standard deviation sigma. P(X>168)=0.35 and P(X>174 | X>168)=0.25. Find mu and sigma. [7]
questions.title: Normal distribution parameters

stem: R(4,-2,6) and S(-2,4,0) are endpoints of a sphere's diameter. Let A=(4,4,6).

parts.label: a
parts.html: Find the centre and radius.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Find the sphere's volume.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Show A lies on the sphere and find angle RAS.

parts.label: d
parts.html: Find the plane through R,S,A and show it contains the centre.

questions.title: Three-dimensional geometry
solution: The centre is C=(1,1,3). CR has length sqrt(27)=3sqrt3, so V=(4/3)pi(3sqrt3)^3=108pi sqrt3. CA also has length sqrt27, so A is on the sphere. AR=(0,-6,0) and AS=(-6,0,-6) have dot product 0, so angle RAS=90 degrees. A normal to the plane is proportional to (1,0,-1), so the plane is x-z=-2; C satisfies 1-3=-2.

stem: At the start of 2026, Maya invests $18 000 at 5.2% nominal annual interest compounded quarterly. Equipment costs $32 000 and depreciates to $29 824 after one year.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Find the investment value at the start of 2031.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Find the annual depreciation rate.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Write models for both values n years after 2026.

parts.label: d
parts.html: Determine the first year Maya can afford the equipment.

questions.title: Compound growth and depreciation
solution: Investment: I_n=18000(1+0.052/4)^(4n). Thus I_5=$23 306. Depreciation factor=29824/32000=0.932, so r=6.8%. Cost C_n=32000(0.932)^n. Solving I_n>=C_n gives the first integer n=5, so Maya can buy it in 2031.

stem: A population is modelled by P(t)=1200/(1+5e^(-0.4t)), t>=0.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Find P(0).

parts.label: b
parts.html: Find when P=800.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Show dP/dt=0.4P(1-P/1200).

parts.label: d
parts.html: Find when the growth rate is greatest and calculate that rate.

parts.label: e
parts.html: State the limiting population.

questions.title: Logistic modelling investigation
solution:
P(0)=1200/6=200. For P=800, 1+5e^(-0.4t)=1.5, so e^(-0.4t)=0.1 and t=ln10/0.4=5.76. Differentiating and substituting P gives P'=0.4P(1-P/1200). This quadratic in P is maximized at P=600. Then
1+5e^(-0.4t)=2, so t=ln5/0.4=4.02, and maximum rate=0.4(600)(1/2)=120 per unit time. The limit is 1200.
